title: Risks to Singapore Economy Given Present External Uncertainty
what_it_is: Risks to Singapore Economy Given Present External Uncertainty

sections.label: US-China trade war questions
sections.summary: Questions ask the Minister for Trade and Industry about the US-China trade war's impact on Singapore and measures to cushion it, noting the IMF lowered global GDP growth forecast.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry (a) whether he can provide an update on the likely impact that Singapore may face from the US-China trade war and the widening reach of US export controls on emerging and foundational technologies; and (b) what measures and policies can be introduced to ensure headwinds from the escalating US-China trade war, disruptions to the global supply chain and global slowdown will not affect our economy significantly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry (a) how will the ongoing trade war between China and the US impact Singapore; (b) whether the Ministry can name the top three things that the man in the street should be prepared for; and (c) how will the Government cushion the impact.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry (a) what are the implications of the trade dispute between the US and China on Singapore's economy; and (b) what are the measures that the Government is prepared to implement should our economy slow down significantly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry (a) what is the Government's assessment of the impact of the US-China trade war on the Singapore economy and which sectors are envisaged to be worst-hit or particularly vulnerable; and (b) what measures will the Government institute to support Singaporean workers in these sectors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry whether he can (i) give an assessment of the risk of a global trade war and (ii) elaborate on the strategies that Singapore is deploying to manage that risk.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has lowered its forecast for global gross domestic product (GDP) growth this year by 0.2 percentage points, from 3.5% to 3.3%.

sections.label: Employment and growth projections
sections.summary: Employment rose in the first quarter while unemployment stayed low at 2.2%, and MTI projected 1.5% to 2.5% growth this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Employment continued to increase in the first quarter of the year, while unemployment remains low at 2.2%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: In May, the Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) projected that our economy would grow between 1.5% and 2.5% this year.

sections.label: IMF estimate on US-China tariffs
sections.summary: The IMF estimated that US-China tariffs could cut global economic output by 0.5 percentage points in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The IMF had estimated that the US-China tariffs could cut global economic output by 0.5 percentage points in 2020.

sections.label: Singapore ranked most competitive economy
sections.summary: Collectively these enable Singapore to be more than the sum of its parts, and IMD recently ranked Singapore the world's most competitive economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Collectively, they enable Singapore to be much more than the sum of its individual parts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: That is why the International Institute for Management Development (IMD) recently ranked Singapore the world’s most competitive economy.

sections.label: Advanced Manufacturing niche areas
sections.summary: In Advanced Manufacturing, new niche areas such as additive manufacturing and advanced materials are being created.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: For example, in Advanced Manufacturing, we are creating new niche areas, such as additive manufacturing and advanced materials.

sections.label: Agri-Food Innovation Park
sections.summary: A new Agri-Food Innovation Park is being established in Sungei Kadut to realise agritech ambitions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: For example, we are establishing a new Agri-Food Innovation Park in Sungei Kadut to realise our agritech ambitions.

sections.label: GSK Singapore investment
sections.summary: GSK is investing more than $100 million in Singapore to produce new medicines faster with a lower carbon footprint.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: GSK is investing more than $100 million in Singapore to produce new medicines faster, with a lower carbon footprint.

sections.label: Scale-up SG programme launch
sections.summary: Enterprise Singapore will launch the Scale-up SG programme on Wednesday to give customised assistance to high potential companies to grow and internationalise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Enterprise Singapore will, therefore, launch the "Scale-up SG" programme on Wednesday to provide customised assistance to high potential companies to grow and internationalise.

sections.label: RCEP free trade area
sections.summary: Once concluded, RCEP will be the world's largest free trade area, covering a third of global GDP and almost half the world's population.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Once concluded, RCEP will be the world's largest free trade area, bringing together economies accounting for a third of the global GDP and almost half of the world's population.

sections.label: Nationalism and protectionism concern
sections.summary: As countries become more nationalistic and take more unilateralist or protectionist measures, it is a concern to all.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: As countries become more nationalistic and undertake more unilateralist or protectionist measures, it is a concern to all.

sections.label: Singapore companies interoperating capabilities
sections.summary: For Singapore to respond, its companies must have real capabilities to interoperate across a more fragmented landscape.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: For Singapore to respond to this scenario, we must make sure that our companies have real capabilities that can allow them to interoperate across a more fragmented landscape.

sections.label: PSA global ports and logistics
sections.summary: Most containers come through Singapore, but changing trade routes and supply chains led PSA to build ports worldwide as a global logistics player.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: So, night, the vast majority of the containers that come to Singapore come through Singapore and we are a major exchange hub.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: But having done that, it is still not sufficient because trade routes might change, and the global supply chains and patterns will also change, which is why, over the years, PSA has built up a string of ports all around the world, allowing them not just to be a port operator, but allowing them to be global logistics players.

sections.label: Budget returns from investment
sections.summary: For every $5 spent in the Budget, slightly more than $1 this year comes from investment returns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Today, we are in a fortunate position whereby for every $5 we spend in the Budget, slightly more than $1 this year comes from our returns from our investment.

sections.label: Economic strategy and external wing
sections.summary: The economic strategy covers growing the external wing, GNP, and mastering investment resources to weather the storm.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: So, going forward, our economic strategy is not just about looking at what we can do domestically, between local firms and foreign firms operating here.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We must also look at how we grow the external wing, our GNP, and how we master our investment resources to make sure that we have the ammunition for us to weather the storm.

sections.label: Export restrictions and technological bifurcation
sections.summary: Restrictions on sensitive technology exports affect the global technological ecosystem and may lead to bifurcation or fragmentation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Indeed, the restrictions on export of what is deemed as a sensitive technology will have implications for the entire global technological ecosystem.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: This is what we call the substitution effect.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: But, in the longer term, what we are most worried about is that it will lead to a bifurcation, if not a fragmentation, of the entire technological space.

sections.label: Singapore strategy to interoperate
sections.summary: Singapore's strategy remains to thrive by interoperating across different jurisdictions and systems.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Our Singapore strategy remains that we will thrive to be able to interoperate across the different jurisdictions and different systems.

sections.label: Singapore and global production shift
sections.summary: Singapore does not compete with regional economies for the entire shift in the global production chain.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Some of it will come to some parts of the region, around here.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: But I must say that Singapore does not compete with the rest of the regional economies for the entire shift in the global production chain.
